audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers hand Lucian the 2+ items row at 7/10 while whys[6], spikes[3] and late all say Ziggs zones him off the map and 'you lose the long game here, plainly'. Levels 4-5 were also marked Lucian while whys[3] says the edge 'narrows to even'.
audit.why: Ziggs is pure artillery — Bouncing Bomb at 850 range on a 4s cooldown at rank 5 and a 5000-range ultimate — against a marksman whose only gap-closer is a 445-range dash. There is no version of two-plus items where Lucian owns the stage.
audit.corrected: 2+ items flipped to Ziggs at 3/10 and Levels 4-5 set to Skill, in both layers.
sources: brief enemyKit Q range 850 cd 6/5.5/5/4.5/4, R range 5000

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0].why claims 'Passive double-shots win level 1 outright' on a row marked Skill, and phases[4]/phases[5] carry the generic Culling and first-item spike lines on rows that are not Lucian's.
audit.why: At 1 Ziggs has one bomb and Lucian has no combo — whys[0] already calls it a wash. At 6 Satchel Charge's knockback can shove Lucian out of the Culling channel, and at one item Ziggs's haste extends the poke rather than Lucian's burst extending its reach.
audit.corrected: All four phase lines rewritten to the real owner of each stage.
sources: brief enemyKit W text (knocks them away), cd 20/18/16/14/12

audit.whatIsWrong: Short Fuse never appears on the page, and the Satchel Charge cooldown is written as 'the fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Short Fuse periodically empowers Ziggs's next basic attack and its cooldown shortens every time he casts a spell, so his burst tell is the attack wind-up rather than an ability cast. Satchel Charge is 20s at rank 1 down to 12s — never fifteen — and that number is the entire green-light system this page is built on.
audit.corrected: dosFull[2] rebuilt around Short Fuse; the real Satchel Charge cooldown added to the cooldown line and to report[5].
sources: brief enemyKit P text + autoReset flag

edits.before: Passive double-shots win level 1 outright — Q through the wave on his last-hits and weave doubletaps on every step-up.
edits.after: Neither of you has a combo at level 1 — Q on his last-hits, take the free chip, and stay out of Bouncing Bomb.

edits.before: Keep the pressure rolling but track Satchel Charge — your lead is HP-bar bullying, not all-in math, until items arrive.
edits.after: He lands Bouncing Bomb more reliably while your mana strains, so your short-trade edge narrows all the way to even.

edits.before: The Culling adds lane-clear and execute chip — use it through walls on recalls and low-HP escapes.
edits.after: The Culling executes a poked Ziggs — but Satchel Charge can knock you clean out of the channel.

edits.before: First item spike is your kill window — the dash-weave combo now deletes half bars. Force the issue before he stabilizes.
edits.after: Your pattern still works at even items, but his first haste item starts extending his poke past your reach.

edits.before: Ziggs burns Satchel Charge on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Short Fuse empowers his next auto — the wind-up is the tell, not the cast.

edits.before: - Ziggs Satchel Charge: matchup-defining — His knockback escape — he is catchable only while it is down. It governs your forward steps. - E dash spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Ziggs Satchel Charge: matchup-defining — his knockback escape, 20s at rank 1 — he is catchable only while it is down. It governs your forward steps. - E dash spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.

edits.before: Track Ziggs’s Satchel Charge: His knockback escape — he is catchable only while it is down. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Ziggs’s Satchel Charge: his knockback escape, 20s at rank 1 — he is catchable only while it is down.

notes: The kit file flags Satchel Charge with 'percentHealth'. Riot's description says only magic damage plus a knockback (and the turret hexplode), so I trusted the description and wrote no percent-health claim — flagging it here as a probable tooltip-parsing misfire. Hexplosive Minefield's 16s flat cooldown and the way successive mine hits on the same target deal reduced damage are both in the kit text and would make good additions to the trading rules, but every candidate field was already at its length ceiling, so I left them for a later pass.
